candidates.source_name: kozadat.hu — Központi Információs Közadat-nyilvántartás (KIK) public search
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory central register (Infotv. + 499/2022. (XII. 8.) Korm. rendelet) into which budgetary bodies, municipalities and minority self-governments must report contracts, subsidies and payments at or above HUF 5 million. This is the single most complete national aggregation of 'szerződések 5 M Ft felett' and therefore captures bank account-management, cash-handling, card-acceptance, POS, payment-processing and IT contracts awarded by public bodies, including many that never appeared as a formal procurement notice.
candidates.source_subtype: government contract register / open data search portal
candidates.access_status: public, no login expected for the search UI
candidates.legal_status: public sector information published under a statutory disclosure duty
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic scripted querying of the composite search (osszetett-kereso) with banking/payment keyword and CPV-style filters; capture result rows + detail pages; check for a bulk/CSV export or an underlying JSON endpoint before resorting to HTML scraping.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on the statutory phrase for the 5 M Ft threshold, then snowballing to the register named in the implementing decree
queries_used: közérdekű adat szerződések 5 millió forint felett közzététel banki szolgáltatás

candidates.why_relevant: Operator-side portal for the Central Information Public Data Registry; documents which organisations are in scope, the reporting data model and the submission schedule. Useful for judging completeness and lag of kozadat.hu records before treating them as evidence of a bank/payments deal.
candidates.access_status: public information pages; data submission requires authentication

candidates.why_relevant: Defines exactly which contract fields must be published, by whom, and with what exemptions (defence, classified, and — contested — bank secrecy). Essential to interpret gaps in the registry rather than mistaking them for absence of deals.

candidates.why_relevant: Central index of the Public Procurement Authority's own databases: the Közbeszerzési Adatbázis (KBA), the CoRe contract repository that replaced KBA for uploading/storing concluded contracts, and the Közbeszerzési Értesítő gazette. candidates.source_name: EKR — Elektronikus Közbeszerzési Rendszer public notice search
candidates.why_relevant: The national e-procurement platform; its unauthenticated public area exposes the contracting-authority register and all procurement notices with CPV codes, buyer name, winning bidder, subject and EKR procedure id. Since the June 2024 upgrade it also offers structured search and email alerting on saved criteria — a ready-made monitoring channel for banking/payment CPVs (66xxxxxx financial services, 30/48xxxxxx POS and payment IT).

candidates.why_relevant: Cleaned, structured, cross-country archive of procurement notices for 33 European states including Hungary, produced by the EU DIGIWHIST project and now maintained by the Budapest-based Government Transparency Institute. Provides buyer/supplier entity pages, award values and corruption-risk indicators, and preserves records whose originals were amended or withdrawn — ideal for longitudinal supplier-share analysis in banking/payments.

The tag pages act as ready-made actor dossiers and surface deals whose original notices are hard to find, making this the fastest entry point into the Hungarian banking-procurement scandal record.

candidates.why_relevant: Public archive of freedom-of-information requests and the authorities' answers, operated by Átlátszó. negative_findings.description: Hungarian case law and practice hold that the Banking Act (Hpt.) is lex specialis to the Info Act, and courts have accepted that the entire contract concluded with a financial institution can fall under bank secrecy (banktitok), so contract data that would otherwise be publishable under the 5 M Ft rule can be withheld precisely when the counterparty is a bank.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches on 'megtagadható-e a banktitoknak minősülő közérdekű adat kiadása' returned legal commentary describing successful refusals on bank-secrecy grounds.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is the single biggest systematic blind spot for this cell: banking and payment contracts are exactly the category most likely to be redacted or withheld in the contract-transparency archives, so absence in kozadat.hu or a body's III.4 list must never be read as absence of a deal.

negative_findings.description: As of August 2026 the Magyar Nemzeti Bank is refusing to release its contracts above HUF 5 million concluded since January 2025, arguing it is not a budgetary body; Transparency International Hungary has complained to NAIH and the case is under investigation.
negative_findings.result_summary: Multiple independent Hungarian outlets (Portfolio, 444, Economx, Contextus) report the refusal and the NAIH complaint.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The central bank — a major buyer of payment infrastructure and financial IT — is currently a hole in the contract-transparency record. The NAIH decision, when it lands, will determine whether a large body of MNB contract data becomes collectable, and should be tracked as a scheduled event.

negative_findings.description: No documented public bulk-download or open API was confirmed for EKR, the Közbeszerzési Hatóság databases (KBA/CoRe), or kozadat.hu during this pass — only human-facing search interfaces and, for EKR, an email notification service.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language query 'EKR nyílt adat letöltés' returned portal and training material but no open-data/API documentation.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design for the national layer will likely depend on scraping or on the EU TED/Opentender mirrors, which have different coverage (TED only above EU thresholds) and different lag. Worth a dedicated verification pass and, if needed, a FOI request via KiMitTud for machine-readable exports.

negative_findings.description: K-Monitor has publicly criticised the new state public-spending database as poor ('lesújtó'), per Szabad Európa reporting on the K-Monitor blog.
negative_findings.result_summary: Found via local-language search; the specific critique post on k.blog.hu was not read in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests the statutory central register (kozadat.hu / KIK) may be incomplete or badly structured; NGO archives should be treated as complements, not fallbacks, and the critique should be read before setting confidence on registry-derived counts.

negative_findings.description: An automated fetch of https://k-monitor.hu/adatbazisok returned HTTP 403 Forbidden.
negative_findings.result_summary: Single failed fetch; other k-monitor.hu and adatbazis.k-monitor.hu URLs appeared normally in search results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Almost certainly bot defence rather than a dead page — recorded as a hypothesis, not a verdict. Collection should use a browser-like client for this domain.

negative_findings.description: The aHáló network database was described on K-Monitor's activities page as 'ahalo.hu', but that hostname was not independently confirmed reachable in this pass, and the seeded alternative 'halo.k-monitor.hu' produced no direct hit.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the K-Monitor descriptive page was confirmed as a search hit.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The candidate is recorded with a reduced confidence score; the deterministic liveness pass should resolve the correct hostname before collection is scheduled.

coverage_gaps.description: Municipality-level contract registers were not enumerated. Hungarian local governments each run their own 'általános közzétételi lista / III.4' page, and municipal account-management and card-acceptance mandates are a core banking market — but this cell only established the generic heading pattern, not a list of the largest municipalities' actual disclosure URLs.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a seed list of the ~30 largest önkormányzatok (plus Budapest districts) and crawl their közérdekű adatok / III.4 pages using the confirmed heading path; note that the Oct-2025 shift of municipal accounts to the Államkincstár changes what will appear going forward.

coverage_gaps.description: Contract disclosures of state-owned banks and financial vehicles (MFB, Eximbank, Magyar Posta / Posta financial services, Diákhitel Központ, MBH as successor of MKB/Budapest Bank/Takarék) were not individually mapped, although K-Monitor tag pages and a Diákhitel 'Közadatkereső' page were observed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate each state-owned financial institution's közérdekű adatok page and its 5 M Ft contract list; treat Diákhitel's Közadatkereső as the template for how these bodies expose the data.

coverage_gaps.description: No audit-institution sources were covered: Állami Számvevőszék (ÁSZ) audit reports on account-management and IT procurement, and Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottság (KDB) remedy decisions, both of which expose contested banking/payment tenders in detail.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a dedicated pass over asz.hu report search and the Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottság decision database on kozbeszerzes.hu, filtered to financial-services and IT subject matter.

coverage_gaps.description: EU-funded contract archives specific to Hungary (palyazat.gov.hu / Széchenyi támogatott projektek lists, EU Financial Transparency System) were not covered, even though they carry a parallel disclosure duty above the same thresholds and often finance digitalisation and payment infrastructure.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add palyazat.gov.hu supported-project lists and data.europa.eu EU-funds datasets as a follow-up cell or extension of this one.

coverage_gaps.description: No company-registry source (Opten, Céginfo, e-cegjegyzek / IM Céginformációs Szolgálat) was assessed, so winning-bidder names from award notices cannot yet be resolved to ownership, financials, or group structure.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assess e-cegjegyzek.hu and at least one commercial registry vendor for licensing terms, then define the join key (adószám / cégjegyzékszám) between award notices and company data.

coverage_gaps.description: The specific CPV code set that delimits banking and payments (e.g. 66100000 banking and investment services, 66110000 banking services, 66172000 financial transaction processing, 30144200 / 30123000 ticketing and cash-register machinery, 48xxxxxx financial software) was reasoned about but not verified against actual Hungarian notices.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a calibration pass on EKR/TED HU notices to confirm which CPV codes Hungarian buyers actually use for account management, card acquiring and POS, then freeze that list as the standing collection filter.

coverage_gaps.description: Hungarian national contract-transparency sources are overwhelmingly Hungarian-only; no English-language mirror of kozadat.hu, EKR or CoRe was found. English coverage exists only at the EU/NGO layer (TED, Opentender, Integrity Watch).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Plan for Hungarian-language parsing and translation in the pipeline rather than assuming an English feed; use TED/Opentender only for above-threshold and cross-country comparison.

brief: Hungary's contract-transparency layer has three tiers: a statutory national one (kozadat.hu / Központi Információs Közadat-nyilvántartás for all contracts at or above HUF 5 million, EKR for procedures and notices, the Közbeszerzési Hatóság's CoRe repository for signed contracts, plus KEF framework agreements and DKÜ for state IT buys), an EU tier (TED bulk XML/OCDS, which reliably captures above-threshold banking and payment awards and is by far the most machine-readable), and a civic-archive tier (K-Monitor's tagged database and aHáló network graph, Transparency International's Tenderbajnok, RedFlags, and Átlátszó's KiMitTud FOI archive) that cleans, links and preserves what the official portals bury or amend. For this sector the decisive caveat is legal: bank secrecy under the Hpt. is treated as lex specialis to the Info Act and has been used successfully to withhold entire contracts with financial institutions, and as of August 2026 the MNB is refusing its own 5 M Ft contract list with a NAIH complaint pending — so silence in the registers is not evidence of no deal. Practically, no confirmed public bulk endpoint was found for the Hungarian national systems, so collection should lean on TED/Opentender for structured history, scripted querying of kozadat.hu, EKR and CoRe for national coverage, and KiMitTud FOI requests as an active channel where proactive publication fails.
